review_output.summary: [High] No test runs the multi-byte branch of the new 7-bit length encoder
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: The test project builds only for net10.0, so every test runs the new NET10_0_OR_GREATER constructor. But every purpose in KeyRingBasedDataProtectorTests.cs is short ASCII (<128 bytes), so nothing runs the while loop in Write7BitEncodedInt and nothing makes Measure7BitEncodedUIntLength return 2 or more. A wrong length prefix for a long purpose would either crash with an IndexOutOfRange or produce a different AAD, so existing cookies and tokens would stop decrypting, and CI would catch neither. Remedy: Add a [Theory] like Protect_EncryptsToDefaultProtector_MultiplePurposes with purposes of UTF-8 length 127, 128, 16383 and 16384, and compare against BuildAadFromPurposeStrings (test line 621), which builds the expected bytes with BinaryWriter.Write(string).

review_output.summary: [Medium] The AAD wire format now has two serializers, split by a TFM gate nothing else in src/ uses
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: One security-sensitive AAD layout is now written by two unrelated code paths: span code with a hand-written varint, and BinaryWriter/MemoryStream with PurposeBinaryWriter. The constructors also take different parameter types (string[] vs IEnumerable<string>). Data protected on one target framework must unprotect on another, yet nothing ties the two paths together, so every future format change has to be made twice and kept byte-identical by hand. NET10_0_OR_GREATER appears nowhere else in src/, while this file uses #if NETCOREAPP / #elif NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK / #else #error at lines 144 and 297. Remedy: Merge into one implementation for all target frameworks (fixed + WriteBigEndianInteger + pointer-based Encoding.GetBytes), deleting the #else branch. At minimum, gate on NETCOREAPP using the file's #elif/#error pattern, give both constructors the same parameter type, and add a test that both paths produce the same bytes.

review_output.summary: [Medium] No test uses non-ASCII purposes, so nothing checks that UTF-8 byte counts (not char counts) are used
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: The new code sizes the buffer and the length prefix from GetByteCount and writes with GetBytes. With all-ASCII test purposes, byte count equals char count, so a regression that used purpose.Length would pass every existing test while breaking AAD compatibility (unprotect failures) for apps with non-ASCII purposes. Remedy: Add purposes such as "pürpose", "目的" and "\U0001F600", plus new string('é', 64) (64 chars but 128 bytes, which pushes the length prefix to 2 bytes), and assert against BuildAadFromPurposeStrings.

review_output.summary: [Medium] Write7BitEncodedInt is a copy of OutputCaching's FormatterBinaryWriter.Write7BitEncodedInt, comments included
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: The repo now has several hand-written 7-bit/VarInt encoders: src/Middleware/OutputCaching/src/FormatterBinaryWriter.cs:140, src/SignalR/common/Shared/BinaryMessageFormatter.cs:20 (an independent implementation, not a BCL copy) and this one. A fix in one copy will not reach the others, and this one is part of the DataProtection AAD wire format, so it must stay byte-identical to BinaryWriter.Write(string). Remedy: Move one span-based Write7BitEncodedInt and its length function into src/Shared/ and link it with <Compile Include="$(SharedSourceRoot)..." LinkBase="Shared" />, the way the csproj already links ArgumentNullThrowHelper.cs. At minimum, add a comment pointing at the existing copy and at the BCL method it mirrors.

review_output.summary: [Low] The rented ArrayPool buffer is not returned on throw, and the header size is written as bare 4 + keySize + 4
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: SecureUtf8Encoding (throwOnInvalidBytes: true) throws on a purpose with a lone surrogate. When that happens, ArrayPool<int>.Shared.Return is never reached and the pooled array is lost to the GC; callers see the same exception as before. The header size 4 + keySize + 4 is repeated with literals, while the rest of the file writes sizeof(uint) + sizeof(Guid). Remedy: Wrap the work in try/finally, or use stackalloc (or simply call GetByteCount again in the write loop). Define one header-size constant from sizeof(uint) + sizeof(Guid) + sizeof(uint).

Impact: Two functions now measure the same VarInt encoding (src/SignalR/common/Shared/BinaryMessageFormatter.cs:41 and this one). If the measure and the writer disagree, the Debug.Assert(index == targetArr.Length) is the only check, and it does nothing in release builds. Remedy: Put the length function in the same shared source file as the consolidated writer, and delete the commented-out loop at lines 407-413.

review_output.summary: [Low] No test covers an empty purpose, the case `value | 1` exists for
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: The `| 1` exists only so a zero-length purpose measures as 1 byte. CreateProtector only rejects null, so "" is a valid purpose, but no test checks that it writes the single 0x00 length byte the old BinaryWriter path wrote; a regression would go unnoticed. Remedy: Add "" as a purpose, alone and mixed with others, to the AAD-equality theory compared against BuildAadFromPurposeStrings.

review_output.summary: [Low] `using System.Buffers.Text` is never used, and the new usings are out of order
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: Nothing in the file uses a System.Buffers.Text type. It sits after the Microsoft.* usings, which breaks dotnet_sort_system_directives_first (.editorconfig:24), and System.Buffers.Binary comes before System.Buffers; it looks pasted in and adds noise. The build is not broken, because IDE0005 is suppressed for multi-targeted projects. Remedy: Delete `using System.Buffers.Text;`, sort the usings (System.Buffers, then System.Buffers.Binary), and add `using System.Numerics;` instead of the fully qualified System.Numerics.BitOperations.

review_output.summary: [Nitpick] The file now writes big-endian uint32 values two ways
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: The new code writes MAGIC_HEADER_V0 with BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian, while the same class still writes and reads the same header field with its own pointer-based WriteBigEndianInteger (:311) and ReadBigEndian32BitInteger (:155). That is two ways to do one job in one class. Remedy: In a follow-up, route those helpers through BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian / ReadUInt32BigEndian, or delete them.

review_output.summary: [Nitpick] Commented-out code after a `return`, plus a comment copied from the BCL
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: The commented-out loop after the return in Measure7BitEncodedUIntLength is dead code that can drift from the live code. The "0x7F and ~0x7F codegen" comment in Write7BitEncodedInt is copied from the BCL. Neither says what the code actually depends on: the output must match BinaryWriter's 7-bit length prefix. Remedy: Replace both with one line saying the encoding must match BinaryWriter's 7-bit length prefix (the #else path) so the AAD bytes stay identical across target frameworks.

result_text:
I sent all 10 findings from the final report to the report tool. The refuted IDE0005 build-break finding was not sent.

**Verdict: BLOCK (code).** The block comes from one verified High: no test runs the long-purpose (128+ byte) length path in the new net10.0 serializer.

The new code writes the same AAD bytes as the old `BinaryWriter` path, which three reviewers checked independently. Everything else found is about maintainability and missing tests, not a bug:

- **Medium:**
  - The AAD format now has two serializers split by a one-off `NET10_0_OR_GREATER` gate.
  - No test uses a non-ASCII purpose.
  - `Write7BitEncodedInt` is copied from OutputCaching.
- **Low (4) and Nitpick (2):** the pooled buffer isn't returned when the constructor throws, a duplicate length helper, no empty-purpose test, an unused and misordered `using`, two ways of writing big-endian values, and commented-out code.

There was no spec to review against: the commits cite no issue, and the PR-body lookup with `gh` wasn't approved.
